chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said:

No child had been born to me at all, and I went out to Makkah and I had no son. A person met me and gave me the good news of a boy. So I passed by and entered upon Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) in Al-Madina. When I came to be in his presence, he said to me: 'How are you, and how is your son?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I went out and I had no son. A neighbor of mine met me and said to me: A boy has been born to you.' He smiled, then said: 'Have you named him?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Name him Ali, for my father, whenever a delay occurred with one of his slave girls, would say to her: O So-and-so, intend (for him) Ali, so it would not be long before she would become pregnant and give birth to a boy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the name Ali in relation to fertility and the Imams' practices?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual efficacy of naming children after the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the name 'Ali' to divine facilitation of progeny. It specifically connects the practice to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), illustrating how the Imams' names carry barakah that influences fertility and lineage. The narrative underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and blessing power inherent in the names of the Imams.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Musa Bin Ja’far, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Amro who said,

‘There were no births for me at all, and I went out to Makkah and there was no child for me. So a person met me and gave me the good news of a boy. So I passed by and went to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> at Al-Medina. So when I came to be in front of him<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘How are you, and how is your son?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I went out and there was no child for me. So a neighbour of mine met me, so he said to me, ‘There has been born a boy for you’. So he<sup>asws</sup> smiled, then said, ‘Have you named him yet?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Name him Ali, for my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, whenever there was a delay by a slave girl from his<sup>asws</sup> slave girls over it, said to her: ‘O so and so! Make the intention (of naming him) Ali’. So it would not be long before she would become pregnant and give birth to a boy’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Musa ibn Ja‘far from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn ‘Umar [‘Amr] who has said the following:

“I never had a child . I went to Makkah and did not have any children. A man met me and gave good news of the birth of a boy to me. I then went on and visited Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. When I went before him (the Imam), he (the Imam) asked, ‘How are you and how is your son?’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I left home but I did not have a son. My neighbor met me and said, “A boy is born to you .’” He (the Imam) smiled and asked, ‘Have you given him a name?’ I replied, ‘No, I have not given him a name.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Name him Ali; whenever a delay would take place in giving birth of any of my father’s girls he would ask her to keep her intention to name him Ali, then without much delay she would give birth to a boy.’”
